title: Elevators existed before Otis; he made them safe to ride
body: Hoists for lifting goods are ancient, but riding one was risky because a snapped rope meant a deadly fall. In the 1850s Elisha Otis developed a safety brake: if the rope lost tension, a spring forced catches into toothed rails beside the platform. At an exhibition in New York in 1854, he rode a platform up and had the rope cut, and it stayed put. Safe passenger elevators helped make tall buildings practical.
